title: How to organise the baking zone | Pantry
description:
Holds everything you need to start a bake without a trip to the shop first.

This is the Baking Zone in the Pantry. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
Flour, sugar and brown sugar in sealed containers you can open one-handed. Baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and yeast together in one small box with their dates showing. Cutters, cases and piping tips in a single lift-out bin, and no loose sprinkles rolling around the shelf.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Test the leaveners rather than guessing: a spoon of baking powder into hot water should fizz hard, and yeast i
Straighten: Build one lift-out bin holding flour, sugar, bicarb, vanilla and a scoop, so starting a bake is one trip to th
Shine: Flour turns to paste under a damp cloth, so brush or vacuum the shelf dry first and wipe afterwards.
Safety: Poison, choke, or strangle: almond meal, nut flours and sesame share this shelf with everything else, and one
Standardize: Write the opening date on the lid of every leavener the day you open it, because the printed date stops meanin
Sustain: When the oven timer goes and the bake comes out to cool, the bin goes back to its shelf with the scoop washed

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
One lift-out baking bin with a washed scoop, leaveners dated on the lid the day they are opened, and allergen flours sealed with a scoop of their own.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/pantry-the-baking-zone.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
